findings.title: Validation side effect increments match_count twice per signup attempt
findings.body:
`BlockedEmail.should_block?` writes to the database: it increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at` and calls `save`. It is called from inside a validator.

`UsersController#create` runs validation twice: once in `user.valid?` (when `call_discourse_hub?` is on) and again in `user.save`. Any other caller of `valid?` also triggers a write. As a result, a single blocked signup attempt is counted two or more times, so the statistics are inaccurate.

Putting persistence side effects in a validator is fragile. Record the match once, explicitly, at the point of the actual signup attempt.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and trivially bypassed
findings.body:
`BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` does an exact, case-sensitive match. The value checked is the raw user-supplied email, and neither the stored email nor the input is normalized.

A blocked address like `bad@spammers.org` can be bypassed by registering `Bad@Spammers.org` or adding surrounding whitespace. Normalize the email (e.g. `Email.downcase(email).strip`) both when storing and when looking up.

findings.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of match_count
findings.body:
`record.match_count += 1; record.save` reads the record, increments the count in Ruby and writes it back. Concurrent signup attempts against the same blocked email can lose increments.

Use an atomic update, e.g. `BlockedEmail.where(id: record.id).update_all(['match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ?', Time.zone.now])`. This also avoids running validations and callbacks just to bump a counter.

findings.title: rejectedEmails array defined on prototype is shared across instances
findings.body:
`rejectedEmails: Em.A([])` inside `extend` creates one array on the class prototype. Every instance of `CreateAccountController` shares and mutates the same array.

Rejected emails therefore persist across modal re-openings and controller instances for the life of the page. Initialize the array per instance instead, e.g. in `init` with `this.set('rejectedEmails', Em.A())`.

findings.title: Any server-side email error permanently marks the email invalid client-side
findings.body:
The client pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` whenever `result.errors.email` is present. Transient or recoverable errors, such as the domain whitelist being changed by an admin, therefore lock that email out for the rest of the session.

After that, the field only shows the generic 'invalid' message. The real server reason appears only in the flash, so users get confusing feedback.

findings.title: Domain restriction regex is unanchored
findings.body:
The regex `@(domains)` built from the setting is not anchored to the end of the string.

With a whitelist of `example.com`, an address like `x@example.com.attacker.net` passes the whitelist. With a blacklist of `mail.ru`, entries also unintentionally match domains like `mail.rux.com`.

The logic was moved from `User` unchanged, but now that it is a reusable validator it should be anchored, e.g. `@(domains)\z`.
